name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
A large batch fixing three separate causes of "everything is duplicated," the seeking/playback-stall bug, and a wrong-duration bug, plus multi-server pools.

Duplicates had two independent root causes. First, PruneServerSources only detected a stale cache entry being superseded by a newer key in the raw-to-provider direction (an item first cached without provider ids, then re-keyed once dedup matched it) - the far more common reverse direction, a provider-keyed entry losing its claim to a raw or different-provider key, was never checked, so the old copy survived forever. Second, and more fundamentally: dedup compares provider ids using the lowercase names in DedupProviderIds ("imdb", "tmdb", "tvdb"), but Jellyfin stamps them Pascal-cased ("Imdb", "Tmdb") on both BaseItem and BaseItemDto, and neither dictionary is guaranteed case-insensitive. A plain TryGetValue("imdb", ...) against a dictionary keyed "Imdb" silently missed every real entry - in three separate places (cross-server dedup, and both directions of "don't federate what's already owned locally"). Dedup had never actually matched anything, ever, regardless of the EnableDedup toggle. Both are fixed: PruneServerSources now checks supersession symmetrically for raw and provider-keyed entries, and a new case-insensitive FederationLibraryManager.TryGetProviderId replaces every raw TryGetValue call. Verified live: 311 stale Movie entries and 27 Shows entries pruned on the first sync after the cache fix; after also fixing the case bug and turning dedup on, a further 30 Movies and 178 Shows items were removed for duplicating content already owned locally.

Seeking (dragging the playback position) reliably stalled or hung forever in Proxy mode. FederationStreamHandler.HandleProxyAsync reported Content-Length as rangeStart plus the remote's partial content length, instead of just the partial length - overstating it by exactly the seek offset on every non-zero-start Range request. A client seeking to byte 1,000,000 of a 6,000,000-byte file would be told the response contained 6,000,000 bytes when only 5,000,000 would ever arrive, and would wait indefinitely for the rest. Only the very first Range: bytes=0- request escaped this by coincidence (0 + length == length), which is why playback could start but stalled on every seek and on ordinary buffer-ahead reads. Fixed to report the response's actual partial length; verified live against a real federated stream that Content-Length now matches Content-Range exactly.

A federated item's displayed duration could be wrong forever with no way to recover. Reconciliation restamps an existing item's stream URL in place when it changes (streaming mode, server address, enabled state), but never touched RunTimeTicks - a value stamped once at item creation from whatever the cache held that sync. If that sync ever returned a bad or short value, the item was stuck showing it permanently, even though the cache's own copy gets corrected on every later sync. Reconciliation now compares and restamps RunTimeTicks the same way it already does for the URL, so a wrong duration self-heals on the next sync instead of requiring a full delete/recreate - watch progress is preserved either way.

Also: the federation badge's cloud icon could appear three or four times per card (matched hover-control buttons and footers sharing the same data-id, not just the poster) - now scoped to exactly the card element. The per-item badge and detail-page pill now name which server content is streamed from. Added multi-server pools: one admin creates a named pool and invites servers into it by URL; accepting an invite (still an ordinary friend-request accept - nothing connects without a human clicking Accept) also introduces the new member to every other pool member automatically, so a pool converges into "everyone federates with everyone" without every pair needing a separate manual introduction.

150 tests (up from 133), including new coverage for the cache-supersession fix, the case-insensitive provider id lookup, the Content-Length fix (proved to fail against the pre-fix code), and pool creation/invite/accept-fan-out.
